**Service Name:** Spotify Terms of Use

These Terms of Service govern your relationship with Spotify and explain how you're allowed to use the company's services, including its music streaming product.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** The Terms apply to Spotify's products and services.
* **Content and License:** When you upload content to Spotify, such as music, playlists, or podcasts, you're granting Spotify the right to use that content to improve its services. The company might use AI (artificial intelligence) to analyze and process your content.
* **Privacy:** The terms don't directly explain how Spotify uses or protects your personal data but instead refer to the company's separate Privacy Policy.
* **Dispute Resolution:** You and Spotify have to go through binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) to resolve disputes. This means you can't file a lawsuit. Most users won't be able to join class-action lawsuits either.
* **Termination:** You or Spotify can terminate the agreement at any time, but the terms don't explain the specific conditions.

**Harmful Clauses:**

* The class-action waiver in the dispute resolution clause might be problematic for users who feel Spotify has unfairly treated them. This clause prevents them from joining a group lawsuit.
* The arbitration clause might make it harder for users to resolve disputes with Spotify.

**What Users Should Know:**

* When you use Spotify, you're giving the company the right to use your uploaded content.
* The Privacy Policy explains how Spotify collects and processes your personal data.
* You can't file a lawsuit against Spotify if there's a dispute.
* Class-action lawsuits might not be an option.
* Either party can terminate the agreement at any time.

**Additional Resources:**

* Spotify's Privacy Policy: explains how the company collects and processes your personal data.
* Contact Information: Find Spotify's legal contact information at [https://www.spotify.com/us/legal/end-user-agreement/](https://www.spotify.com/us/legal/end-user-agreement/).
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — SPOTIFY TERMS OF USE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Spotify and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added language for AI-generated playlists/'AI DJ', expanded the User Content license to cover user-uploaded audio/podcasts processed by AI features, and updated arbitration and class-action waiver clauses.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Spotify to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.spotify.com/us/legal/end-user-agreement/ . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.spotify.com/us/legal/end-user-agreement/ .

**Netflix Terms of Use Summary**

This document outlines the terms and conditions for using Netflix's services. Here's a breakdown of the key provisions:

**Service Name:**
Netflix provides streaming services for movies, TV shows, and other content through its online platform.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** These terms apply to all users of Netflix services.
* **Content and License:** Netflix can use user-submitted content, such as ratings and reviews, to improve and train its AI/ML systems.
* **Privacy:** Netflix's published Privacy Policy outlines how personal data is collected and processed.
* **Dispute Resolution:** Most users are required to use binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) to resolve disputes. This includes a class-action waiver, which means users cannot join a group lawsuit.
* **Termination:** Either party can terminate the agreement, subject to the conditions outlined in the document.
* **Contact:** For questions about these terms, users should visit Netflix's official help website at https://help.netflix.com/legal/termsofuse.

**Potential Red Flags:**

* **Dispute Resolution:** The requirement for binding arbitration and class-action waiver may limit users' ability to seek compensation or justice in court.
* **Termination:** Users should be aware that Netflix can terminate the agreement, which may affect their access to content and services.
* **Data Use:** While Netflix's Privacy Policy outlines personal data collection, users should be aware that their data may be used to improve and train AI/ML systems.

It's essential to review the full document and Netflix's Privacy Policy to understand the terms and conditions of using their services.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — NETFLIX TERMS OF USE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Netflix and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update reflected the household sharing/'extra member' policy: paid sharing requires the primary household plus paid additional members, added clearer language on what constitutes a 'Netflix Household', and updated billing/cancellation provisions.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Netflix to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://help.netflix.com/legal/termsofuse . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://help.netflix.com/legal/termsofuse .

**Disney+ Subscriber Agreement**

These Terms of Service govern your relationship with Disney+ and apply to the products and services described on our official terms page.

**Key Provisions:**

* The service may show ads on all tiers, even those labeled "ad-free" or "no ads".
* User-submitted content may be used to improve and train artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) systems, subject to your settings and applicable law.
* Your personal data is collected and processed according to Disney's published Privacy Policy, which you can find linked in these Terms.
* Disputes must be resolved through binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court), with some exceptions (you can opt out of this process within 30 days of opening a new account).
* Either you or Disney can terminate the agreement, subject to conditions outlined in the live document.

**Flags for Harmful Clauses:**

* The inclusion of ads on what were previously labeled "ad-free" or "no ads" tiers may be a concern for users who paid extra to avoid ads.
* The use of user-submitted content to train AI/ML systems may raise concerns about data protection and potential misuse of user information.
* The move to binding arbitration for dispute resolution may be seen as limiting users' access to the court system and creating barriers to seeking redress.

Note that these flags are based on changes and provisions in the updated Terms of Service and may not be exhaustive.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — DISNEY+ SUBSCRIBER AGREEMENT (Effective 2025; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Disney+ and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2025 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: Effective January 27, 2025 for new subscribers and March 24, 2025 for existing ones: streaming titles may now show ads even on 'no ads'/'ad free' tiers, expanded arbitration with mass-arbitration procedures following Disney's earlier 2024 Wrongful-Death-case controversy, and updated content-availability language.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Disney+ to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.disneyplus.com/legal/subscriber-agreement . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20240101000000*/https://www.disneyplus.com/legal/subscriber-agreement .

response:
**Service Name:** PayPal User Agreement

The PayPal User Agreement governs the relationship between PayPal and its users. This is an updated version of the contract (effective 2024).

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** These terms apply to all PayPal products and services mentioned on their official terms page.
* **Content and License:** PayPal can use user-submitted content (e.g., reviews, ratings) to improve their services, AI, and machine learning. However, they will follow the user's settings and applicable laws regarding this use.
* **Privacy:** PayPal's terms reference their published Privacy Policy, which explains how personal data is collected and processed.
* **Dispute Resolution:** Most users must agree to binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with class-action waivers. This means users cannot participate in a class action lawsuit. However, new accounts have 30 days to opt out.
* **Termination:** Either PayPal or the user can terminate the agreement, but the terms of termination are described in the live document.
* **Contact:** For questions, check PayPal's published legal contact information.

**Clauses to Consider Carefully:**

2. WHAT CHANGED. PayPal publishes upcoming and historical policy diffs at paypal.com/us/legalhub/policy-updates.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by PayPal to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.

6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.paypal.com/us/legalhub/useragreement-full . The previous version is available at https://www.paypal.com/us/legalhub/upcoming-policies-full .

**Service Name: eBay User Agreement**

The eBay User Agreement (Effective 2024) governs your relationship with eBay and applies to various products and services listed on their official terms page.

**Key Provisions:**

- **Scope**: These terms apply to all users, and they govern eBay's relationships with its users.
- **Content and License**: eBay uses user-submitted content, such as listings, to improve and train their AI/ML systems, as long as you allow them to do so in your account settings.
- **Payment**: eBay manages payments for transactions, but the specifics of this process aren't detailed in these terms.
- **Privacy**: eBay collects and processes your personal data according to their published Privacy Policy, which details what data is collected and how it's handled.
- **Dispute Resolution**: Most issues are resolved through binding arbitration, which means bypassing the court system. This requires you to opt-out within 30 days of signing up, and this clause can be a concern for some users. (Note: Arbitration is a private dispute process instead of going to court.)
- **Termination**: Either you or eBay can end the agreement if necessary, according to the conditions in the live document.
- **Contact**: If you have questions about these terms, look at eBay's official legal contact information.

**Potential Concerns:**

- **Arbitration and Dispute Resolution**: This clause could limit your abilities to take eBay to court, and the requirement to opt-out within 30 days might be a challenge for some users.

It's essential to read these terms thoroughly and consider seeking guidance if you have specific concerns about the user agreement.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — EBAY USER AGREEMENT (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with eBay and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update revised payments-on-eBay structure for managed payments, added more detailed AI/automated-decision sections, expanded permitted-use language for listing data, and updated arbitration / opt-out procedures.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by eBay to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.ebay.com/help/policies/member-behaviour-policies/user-agreement?id=4259 . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.ebay.com/help/policies/member-behaviour-policies/user-agreement?id=4259 .

**Service Name:** Amazon Conditions of Use (as of 2024)

These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Amazon and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page. Here's a breakdown of the key provisions:

### Scope
These conditions apply to all products and services offered by Amazon that are listed on the company's official terms page.

### Content and License
* When you submit content to Amazon (like posting a review or picture), you agree that Amazon can use it to operate, improve, or train their Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) systems, subject to your privacy settings and the law.
* This might mean that your content helps Amazon's AI systems become more accurate, but it might also raise concerns about how your contributions are used.

### Privacy
The terms refer to Amazon's separate **Privacy Policy**, which explains how the company collects, stores, and uses your personal data.

### Dispute Resolution
* If you have a dispute with Amazon, you may have to go through **binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court)** with a class-action waiver. This means you can't join a group lawsuit with others who have similar claims.
* You have a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts to opt-out of this requirement. However, Steam (owned by Valve) has exempted itself from this rule, requiring Amazon to negotiate disputes through the court.

### Harmful Clauses
While these terms are standard, one clause may cause concern:

* **Dispute Resolution**: As mentioned, the inclusion of a class-action waiver in the arbitration process can be seen as limiting users' right to seek justice as a collective group. This can leave individuals with limited options and make it harder to hold large companies accountable for wrongdoing.

### Other Points to Note
* Amazon may **terminate the agreement** if either party decides to do so, but the conditions will depend on the live document.
* For any questions or issues, refer to the **contact information** at the new TOS URL.

It's essential to keep these factors in mind when creating or consuming content within Amazon services.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — AMAZON CONDITIONS OF USE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2022 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Amazon and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2022 version in the following ways: May 2024 update revised disputes/arbitration to explicitly permit small-claims-court actions, updated language about Amazon services covered, and added clearer references to AI features (Alexa, Rufus) and how generated content interacts with the user agreement.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Amazon to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.amazon.com/gp/help/customer/display.html?nodeId=508088 . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20220101000000*/https://www.amazon.com/gp/help/customer/display.html?nodeId=508088 .

**Key Provisions:**

* _Scope_: These terms cover your relationship with Apple and apply to products and services listed on their official terms page.

* _Termination_: Either Apple or you can terminate the agreement under specific conditions (see the live document).
* _Contact_: For questions, visit the provided Apple website or contact them using the listed information.

**Points to Consider:**

* Apple uses your content for various purposes, and while it respects your settings, it seems to prioritize improving its AI and ML systems.
* The arbitration clause may be problematic for some users, as it involves resolving disputes in private and waives class-action suits.
* Apple can terminate the agreement under specific conditions, so users should review these provisions carefully.

**Important Notes:**

* These terms are subject to change, so users should review the latest updates.
* Apple's contact information and the previous version of the Terms of Service are available for reference.

If you're concerned about the mandatory arbitration clause or any other aspect of these Terms, it's essential to review them carefully and consider speaking with a lawyer or a technology expert for guidance.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — ICLOUD TERMS AND CONDITIONS (Effective 2024; replaces the 2022 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Apple and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2022 version in the following ways: 2024 update added Advanced Data Protection (end-to-end encryption) language, references to Apple Intelligence Private Cloud Compute, and revised provisions about how stored content may be accessed by Apple for legal/safety reasons.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Apple to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/icloud/en/terms.html . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20220101000000*/https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/icloud/en/terms.html .

**Service Name:** Snap (Snapchat) Terms of Service

**Plain Language Summary:**

The Snap Terms of Service outline the rules and responsibilities of using the Snapchat service. Here's a breakdown of the key provisions:

### Scope and Content

The Terms apply to the Snapchat service and its products, which you can find on the official terms page. They govern your relationship with Snap, which includes how user-submitted content is used. **(Note: If you submit content, make sure to understand how Snap will use it to operate and improve its AI/ML systems.)**

### Content and License

When you submit content, like photos or videos, you have certain settings that control how Snap uses it. The Terms describe how Snap uses these contents, subject to your settings and applicable law.

### Privacy

The Terms refer to Snap's published Privacy Policy, which explains the types of personal data collected and how it's processed. **(Please review the Privacy Policy to understand what data is being collected.)**

### Dispute Resolution

The Terms require **binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court)** with class-action waivers. This means you can't join a group lawsuit with others who have similar complaints. You have a **30-day opt-out window for new accounts**, but you'll still need to contact Snap during this time if you want to opt out.

### Termination

Either party can terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.

### Contact

If you have questions about these Terms, you can find Snap's contact information at the provided URL.

**Red Flags for Users:**

* **Mandatory arbitration (binding arbitration) with class-action waivers**: These provisions may limit your ability to participate in a group lawsuit or seek damages in court.
* **Data collection and use**: Review the Privacy Policy to understand what data is being collected and how it's being used.

Remember, these Terms can change, so always review them before sharing content or engaging with the service. If you're unsure about any part of the Terms, consider reaching out to the contact information provided.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — SNAP TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2025; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Snap (Snapchat) and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2025 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: Effective April 7, 2025: added new sections on My AI and other generative-AI features, expanded the user-content license for Live/Local/crowd-sourced services, clarified data-sharing with parents (for under-18 users via Family Center), and updated arbitration pre-dispute notice procedures.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Snap (Snapchat) to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.snap.com/terms . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20240101000000*/https://www.snap.com/terms .

The Terms of Service, also known as the "Pinterest Terms of Service," govern your relationship with the Pinterest platform. 

**Key Provisions:**

### Relationship with Pinterest

These terms outline the agreement between you and Pinterest. Key points include:

* These terms apply to all Pinterest products and services.
* Pinterest can use content from your public Pins to train AI/ML models for recommendations and safety (more on this below).

### Content and Licensing

When you post content on Pinterest, you grant Pinterest permission to use it as follows:
#### * Permitted uses:*
 - Operating, improving, and training AI/ML systems.
- Subject to your settings and applicable law.
#### Notable use: 
Using your public Pin content to train AI/ML models for recommendations and safety (as mentioned above).

### Privacy 

The Terms of Service cross-reference Pinterest's published **Privacy Policy**. This policy explains the categories of personal data collected and how it's processed.

### Dispute Resolution

In the event of a dispute, most of the updated terms require **binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court)**, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts. Class-action waivers apply.

### Termination 

Either you or Pinterest can terminate the agreement under the conditions described in the **live document**. 

### Notability:
When reading the entire agreement for these terms, please note that "Steam (Valve)" has removed mandatory arbitration for 2024.

#### **Harmful Clauses:**

* **Arbitration Clause** with a class-action waiver: In the event of a dispute, you might not have the right to participate in a class-action lawsuit against Pinterest. You have a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.
* **AI/ML-powered recommendation system**: Using public Pin content to train AI/ML models for recommendations and safety may be seen as a means to capture and interpret your user data.
* **Private Dispute Resolution:** If a conflict arises, the Terms of Service require arbitration instead of resorting to a public court.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — PINTEREST TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Pinterest and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added language permitting Pinterest to use public Pin content to train AI/ML models for recommendations and safety, clarified obligations for advertisers and merchants, and updated arbitration provisions. Pinterest publishes a public archive at policy.pinterest.com/en/terms-archive.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Pinterest to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://policy.pinterest.com/en/terms-of-service . The previous version is available at https://policy.pinterest.com/en/terms-archive .

Here's a summary of Tumblr's Terms of Service:

**Service Name:** Tumblr is a social media blogging platform and community.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** These Terms govern your relationship with Tumblr and apply to all products and services offered by the company.
* **Content and License:** When you upload content to Tumblr, you grant the company permission to use it to operate and improve its services, including AI and machine learning systems. However, you can control how your content is shared by adjusting your settings.
* **Privacy:** Tumblr's Privacy Policy outlines what personal data is collected and how it's processed. (Please note that the Terms of Service don't provide further details.)
* **Dispute Resolution:** Most provisions in this version of the Terms require you to use binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) for any disputes. There's a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.
* **Termination:** Either Tumblr or you can terminate this agreement under specific conditions.
* **Contact:** For questions or concerns, please visit Tumblr's published legal contact information.

**Red Flags:**

* **Mandatory Arbitration:** The Terms require binding arbitration for disputes, which means you may give up your right to a court trial. (Consider reviewing the 30-day opt-out window carefully.)
* **Limited Control:** While you can adjust your settings to control content sharing, this may not give you complete control over how your data is used.
 
Please review the Terms carefully to understand your rights and responsibilities. If you have concerns, Tumblr provides contact information for questions and support.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — TUMBLR TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Tumblr and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update reflected Automattic's deal to share public Tumblr posts with AI partners (e.g. for training): added language confirming use of public content for AI training and added a user-facing opt-out (Settings > Visibility > Prevent third-party sharing).
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Tumblr to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.tumblr.com/policy/en/terms-of-service . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.tumblr.com/policy/en/terms-of-service .

SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — DROPBOX TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Dropbox and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: Late-2023/early-2024 update added Dropbox AI features (Dropbox Dash, AI search/summary). After user backlash, Dropbox amended language (Dec 2023 / 2024) to explicitly state customer data is not used to train third-party AI models without consent.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Dropbox to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.dropbox.com/terms . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230601000000*/https://www.dropbox.com/terms .

The service in question is Canva's Terms of Use, a set of rules that govern how users engage with their platform. Canva provides a variety of digital tools and services for creative projects.

The key provisions of Canva's Terms of Use can be summarized as follows:

### Service Overview

* The terms apply to all Canva products and services.
* They regulate the user's relationship with Canva.

### User Content

* Canva uses user-submitted content to improve and train their AI/ML systems.
* The platform may share or use content to a certain extent, based on user settings and applicable law.

### Dispute Resolution

* Canva's arbitration policy involves binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court).
* Class-action waivers mean that users can't join together to file a single lawsuit against Canva.
* The arbitration policy includes a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.

### Termination

* Either party can terminate the agreement under certain conditions.
* The details of the termination process are outlined in the live document.

### Contact Information

* Users can find Canva's contact information on their website.

**Clauses that may be considered unfavorable to users:**

* The arbitration policy, which allows Canva and users to resolve disputes in private arbitration instead of going to court.
* The class-action waiver, which prevents users from bringing a group lawsuit against Canva.

Overall, the Canva Terms of Use outline the company's obligations and user responsibilities, including the use of user content and dispute resolution. While the terms are complex, understanding them can help users navigate Canva's platform and protect their rights as users.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — CANVA TERMS OF USE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Canva and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added rules for Canva's generative AI tools (Magic Studio): users own outputs subject to platform rights, restrictions on using Canva-generated content to train other AI models, and new content-moderation/labeling requirements.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Canva to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.canva.com/policies/terms-of-use/ . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.canva.com/policies/terms-of-use/ .

**Service Name:** Notion Terms of Service

**Summary:**

These Terms of Service outline the rules and agreements between you (the user) and Notion, the company that provides its products and services. The main points are:

* **Scope:** These terms apply to the Notion products and services described on the company's official terms page.
* **Content and License:** Notion uses your content to operate, improve, and train its AI/ML systems, subject to your settings and applicable law. 
* **Privacy:** This version of the terms cross-references Notion's published Privacy Policy, which explains what personal data is collected and how it is processed.
* **Dispute Resolution:** You and Notion will resolve disputes through binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court). Most users will not be able to join a class-action lawsuit with others who have similar issues.
* **Termination:** Either you or Notion can terminate the agreement if you follow the conditions in the live document.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Notion AI:** The 2024 update has provisions related to Notion AI, including input/output ownership and the default restriction that Notion will not train foundational models on your data.
* **Data-Residency Options:** If you're on an enterprise plan, the updated terms clarify your options for data residency.
* **Notice and Opt-out:** You have a 30-day window to opt out of binding arbitration if you've just created an account, although the exception is for users who have purchased from a specific company called Steam (Valve).

**Harmful Clauses:**

* **Class-action waivers:** This means that you may not be able to join a class-action lawsuit with others who have experienced similar issues if you accept the terms of service.
* **Data processing:** Notion collects and processes personal data, and you should review the company's Privacy Policy to understand the details.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — NOTION TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Notion and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added Notion AI provisions (input/output ownership, no training of foundational models on customer data by default), updated subprocessor list, and clarified data-residency options for enterprise plans.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Notion to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.notion.com/terms . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.notion.so/terms .

SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — FIGMA TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Figma and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added Figma AI features (Make Designs, Visual Search) provisions, clarified that customer file content is not used to train third-party generative models without opt-in, and updated security and incident-notification language.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Figma to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.figma.com/legal/tos/ . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.figma.com/tos/ .

response:
These are the Terms of Service for the Stack Overflow Public Network. Here's a plain-language summary of the key provisions:

**Service Name:** Stack Overflow Public Network

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** These terms govern your relationship with Stack Overflow and apply to the company's products and services, as listed on their official terms page.
* **Content and License:** When you submit content (e.g., questions and answers), you grant Stack Overflow a license to use it, subject to your settings and applicable law. Stack Overflow uses this content to improve and train its AI and machine learning systems.
* **Privacy:** The terms cross-reference Stack Overflow's published Privacy Policy, which explains what personal data is collected and how it's processed.
* **Dispute Resolution:** You and Stack Overflow agree to binding arbitration (a private dispute process) instead of going to court. Additionally, most contracts in this set have class-action waivers, which can limit your ability to sue as part of a group. However, there is a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.
* **Termination:** Either you or Stack Overflow can terminate the agreement, subject to the conditions described in the live document.

**Clauses that may be harmful to the user:**

* The Class-Action Waiver in the Dispute Resolution provision may limit your ability to sue as part of a group.
* The binding arbitration provision, while optional, may require you to give up your right to a jury trial or to sue in court.
* There is no clear explanation of the "Commercial Agreement" required for bulk extraction of posted content for AI training without explicit permission. This may imply that users cannot use Stack Overflow's content for commercial purposes without a license.
* The termination provision allows Stack Overflow to terminate the agreement under undisclosed conditions, which may harm users who have invested in the platform.
* While the terms say "applicable law" governs your interactions with Stack Overflow, there's no explanation of what this means for specific jurisdictions. This may result in unclear or inconsistent application of the law.

Keep in mind that these terms are subject to change, and the service name and other details may be updated.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — STACK OVERFLOW PUBLIC NETWORK TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Stack Overflow and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: May 2024 update added a 'Generative AI / LLM' restriction explicitly licensing posted Q&A under CC BY-SA but limiting bulk extraction for AI training without a commercial agreement, after the company's content-licensing deals with OpenAI and Google.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Stack Overflow to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://stackoverflow.com/legal/terms-of-service/public . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://stackoverflow.com/legal/terms-of-service/public .

The Terms of Service belong to "Quora," a platform where users can share knowledge and interact with each other.

Here's a summary of the key provisions:

**Scope**: These Terms of Service (TOS) apply to all Quora products and services listed on the company's official terms page.

**Content and License**: When you submit content to Quora, you agree that it can be used by the company to improve and train its AI/ML systems, as long as your account settings and applicable laws allow it. However, it's not entirely clear which specific rights the company gains from this provision.

**Privacy**: Quora cross-references its published Privacy Policy, which explains what personal data the company collects and how it's processed. This might be useful for understanding what data Quora collects, but we can't evaluate the policy's effectiveness since we're not looking at it directly here.

**Dispute Resolution**: If you have a dispute with Quora, most of these terms require **binding arbitration** (a private dispute process instead of a public court), which means you'll need to resolve the issue outside of a courtroom. There's also a **class-action waiver**, meaning you can't join a group lawsuit against Quora. However, if you have a new Quora account and act within a 30-day window, you can opt out of this requirement. Steam (Valve) excluded itself from the mandatory arbitration, but it's not clear why.

**Termination**: Either Quora or you can terminate this agreement if you follow the outlined conditions.

**Contact Information**: If you need help with the TOS, refer to the company's published contact information at the provided link: https://www.quora.com/about/tos

Harmful clauses for users:

* **Class-action waiver**: This clause prevents you from joining a class-action lawsuit against Quora, even if many other users are also affected.
* **Forced arbitration**: The required binding arbitration process may not be as effective as a public court in your favor. Additionally, you're giving up the right to sue Quora in a public court.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — QUORA TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Quora and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added rules for Poe (Quora's AI chatbot platform): user prompts/responses may be used to improve Poe and partner models subject to settings, added bot-developer terms, and revised dispute resolution.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Quora to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.quora.com/about/tos . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.quora.com/about/tos .

The Terms of Service govern your relationship with **23andMe**. Here's a breakdown of the key provisions and potential limitations:

**Scope**: These Terms apply to your use of the products and services listed on **23andMe**'s official terms page.

**Content and License**: When you provide content, like genetic data, to **23andMe**, they can use it to operate and improve their services, including training their AI and machine learning systems. You have control over how your data is used, but the company's main priority is to use it in a way that benefits their business.

**Privacy**: **23andMe** references their published Privacy Policy (available at [link](https://www.23andme.com/legal/privacy-policy/)) to describe the personal data they collect and how it's processed.

**Dispute Resolution**: If you have a dispute with **23andMe**, you'll need to use **binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court)**. This means you waive your right to sue in court. **Harmful clause: The mandatory arbitration requirement and class-action waiver may limit your ability to seek redress for a breach.** However, there's a 30-day opt-out window when you create your account, and you can choose not to opt in.

**Termination**: Either **23andMe** or you can cancel the agreement, but there are conditions that apply.

**Important contact info**: For questions about the Terms of Service, please visit **23andMe**'s official legal page.

In summary, the **23andMe** Terms of Service:

* Set out the scope of the service and its terms
* Allow **23andMe** to use user-submitted content to enhance their business
* Reference the company's published Privacy Policy for data handling
* Mandate binding arbitration and class-action waivers for dispute resolution
* Allow for termination with certain conditions
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — 23ANDME TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2023; replaces the 2022 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with 23andMe and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2023 version differs from the 2022 version in the following ways: After the October 2023 data breach, 23andMe updated its TOS to add a mandatory-arbitration clause and 30-day opt-out window, requiring users who didn't write to opt out to arbitrate any breach-related claims; also limited class-action rights and shortened the dispute-notice window.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by 23andMe to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.23andme.com/legal/terms-of-service/ . The previous version is available at https://www.23andme.com/legal/terms-of-service/full-version/2.0/ .

**Twitch Terms of Service Summary**

Twitch's Terms of Service govern your relationship with the company when using their products and services, such as live streaming and watching videos.

**Key Provisions:**

* **How Your Content is Used:** Twitch can use, share, and distribute your submitted content to operate their platform, improve their services, and train their AI/ML systems (this happens in accordance with your settings and applicable laws).
* **Privacy:** Twitch's privacy policy explains what personal data is collected and how it's processed. The Terms of Service don't provide detailed information on this.
* **Dispute Resolution:** If there's an issue, most cases will go to binding arbitration, where a private judge instead of a court decides the outcome. Class-action lawsuits are not allowed. There's a 30-day window for new accounts to opt out of this process.
* **Termination:** You or Twitch can end your agreement at any time, but the conditions for doing so are outlined in the live document (which you should read carefully).

**Important Clauses:**

* **Class-Action Waivers:** If you have a dispute with Twitch, you won't be able to join a class-action lawsuit with others who have similar issues. You'll have to opt out of arbitration to pursue this option.
* **Binding Arbitration:** This means that a private judge will decide the outcome of disputes, instead of a court. This can be binding and limiting for users.
* **Dispute Resolution:** Be aware that Twitch has specified the dispute-resolution process, which may limit your ability to seek redress for certain issues.

**Additional Information:** 

To understand the company's data collection and privacy practices, you'll need to read Twitch's published Privacy Policy. For questions about these Terms or more information on arbitration, see the company's published contact information on the Twitch website.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — TWITCH TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Twitch and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added new Branded Content disclosure rules, expanded the User Content license to support clips, replays and AI-generated highlights, and updated the dispute-resolution mass-arbitration procedure.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Twitch to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.twitch.tv/p/legal/terms-of-service/ . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.twitch.tv/p/legal/terms-of-service/ .

The document outlines the terms of use for Roblox.

**Key Provisions**

* **Scope**: These terms apply to your relationship with Roblox, which includes their products and services.
* **Content and License**: When you submit content on Roblox, they use it to improve their services and train their AI/ML systems, following your settings and applicable law. (Note that if you have concerns about data use, review the company's published Privacy Policy.)
* **Dispute Resolution**: Most issues will be resolved through binding arbitration with class-action waivers (meaning you won't be part of a larger group lawsuit). You have 30 days to opt out of this requirement when creating a new account.
* **Termination**: You or Roblox can end the agreement, subject to the conditions outlined in the document.
* **Contact**: For questions and concerns, refer to Roblox's contact information listed in the document.

**Harmful Clauses**

SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — ROBLOX TERMS OF USE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Roblox and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update strengthened minor-protection language (default-private accounts under 13, parental-consent flows), updated Robux/DevEx provisions, added rules for Roblox's generative-AI 'Studio Assistant' and avatar-creation tools, and revised arbitration class-waiver section.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Roblox to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://en.help.roblox.com/hc/en-us/articles/115004647846 . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://en.help.roblox.com/hc/en-us/articles/115004647846 .

**Service Name:** Steam Subscriber Agreement (for the Steam platform and its products and services).

**Summary of Key Provisions:**

1. **Relationship with Valve (Steam):** These terms govern your relationship with Steam (Valve), which provides various products and services through the official terms page.
2. **User Content:** Steam uses your submissions (e.g., game reviews, AI training data) to operate its services, following your settings and local laws.
3. **Privacy:** Your personal data is processed in accordance with Steam's published Privacy Policy.
4. **Disputes:** You have a 30-day window to opt out from mandatory binding arbitration (a private dispute resolution process instead of going to court), which typically includes a class-action waiver (preventing group lawsuits).
5. **Termination:** Either party can cancel the agreement under specified conditions.

**Caution:**

* Arbitration and class-action waivers: Steam has removed mandatory arbitration for disputes involving this agreement as of September 26, 2024, but users are still subject to these provisions with newer Steam accounts (30-day opt-out period) and may be restricted in how they can resolve disputes with Steam.
* Users are advised to familiarize themselves with Steam's Privacy Policy to understand the data being collected and how it's processed.

**Contact and Resource Information:**

For questions about these terms, refer to Steam's published legal contact information on the Steam Subscriber Agreement webpage (https://store.steampowered.com/subscriber_agreement/).
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — STEAM SUBSCRIBER AGREEMENT (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Steam (Valve) and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: September 26, 2024 update removed the mandatory arbitration / class-action waiver clauses entirely - Valve now requires disputes to be filed in court (subject to venue rules), reversing several years of arbitration-only language.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Steam (Valve) to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://store.steampowered.com/subscriber_agreement/ . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://store.steampowered.com/subscriber_agreement/ .

**Service Name:** Epic Games Terms of Service

**Summary:** These Terms of Service govern your relationship with Epic Games and its products and services. Here are the key provisions:

* The Terms cover Epic Games' relationship with you, the user, and apply to all products and services listed on the Epic Games official terms page.
* When you submit content, such as in-game creations or User-Generated Content (UGC), Epic Games has the right to use and improve its AI and ML systems with your content, subject to your settings and applicable law.
* Your use of Epic Games' products and services is tied to the company's published Privacy Policy, which explains how your personal data is collected and processed.
* Any disputes or issues between you and Epic Games must go through binding arbitration, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts. This means you may give up your right to take Epic Games to court.
* Epic Games or you can terminate the agreement under certain conditions.

**Harmful Clauses:** 

* **Arbitration with Class-Action Waivers**: The Terms require binding arbitration, which means you'll resolve disputes outside of court. There's also a class-action waiver, which prevents you from joining a group of people with similar disputes against Epic Games. While arbitration can be a fair process, class-action waivers can limit your ability to hold companies accountable for collective wrongdoing.
* **Data Processing**: The Terms allow Epic Games to use your user-submitted content for its AI and ML systems. While this might be beneficial for improving the service, it also means your content may be used without your explicit consent.

**Additional Notes:**

* **Termination**: The Terms allow either party to terminate the agreement under certain conditions. However, the exact terms of termination are not explicitly stated in the provided text.
* **Consumer Rights**: The Terms reference EU-specific consumer rights, but the specific language is not provided.

It's essential to review the Terms of Service carefully and consider the implications of each provision.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — EPIC GAMES TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Epic Games and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update revised the Fortnite/Epic Account language, added User-Generated Content (UEFN) provisions and creator-payout rules, updated EU-specific consumer-rights language post-DMA, and refreshed dispute-resolution sections.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Epic Games to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.epicgames.com/site/en-US/tos . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.epicgames.com/site/en-US/tos .

**Service Name:** DoorDash Consumer Terms of Service

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** These terms govern your relationship with DoorDash for using its products and services.
* **Content and License:** You grant DoorDash permission to use your content, such as order history, for improving its services, subject to your settings and applicable laws.
* **Dispute Resolution:** Most disputes must be resolved through **binding arbitration** (a private dispute process instead of court), with a **30-day opt-out window** for new accounts. This means you (or DoorDash) may not sue each other in court for disputes.
* **Termination:** Either party can terminate the agreement subject to certain conditions.
* **Contact:** If you have questions about these terms, contact DoorDash through its published legal contact information.

**Clauses that May be Harmful to the User:**

* **Binding Arbitration:** This means you may not have a right to a jury trial or lawsuit in court. If you want to opt-out of arbitration, you must do so within 30 days of creating your account.
* **Class-Action Waivers:** Arbitration clauses often include class-action waivers, which mean you cannot join a group lawsuit with others who have similar claims.

**Other Notes:**

* DoorDash's published **Privacy Policy** sets out how your personal data is collected and processed.
* The terms describe how DoorDash uses **AI/ML systems**, including user-submitted content for training and improvement.
* **DashPass auto-renewal** is clarified, but the specific details are not explained here.
* **AI-generated menu summaries** and **order-suggestion features** are new topics covered in the updated terms.
* **Tipping/refund mechanics** have been updated, but the specific changes are not explained here.
* The terms are subject to **applicable law**, which means your local laws may affect the interpretation and enforcement of these terms.

Please note that these terms are subject to change, and you should always review your agreement before using the service.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — DOORDASH CONSUMER TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with DoorDash and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update revised arbitration provisions (including mass-arbitration handling), added DashPass auto-renewal clarifications, updated tipping/refund mechanics and added new sections covering AI-generated menu summaries and order-suggestion features.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by DoorDash to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://help.doordash.com/consumers/s/article/DoorDash-Consumer-Terms-of-Service . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://help.doordash.com/consumers/s/article/DoorDash-Consumer-Terms-of-Service .

**Service Name:** Uber US Terms of Use (effective 2024)

**Key Provisions:**

* These terms govern your relationship with Uber and apply to Uber's products and services listed on their official terms page.
* User-submitted content may be used by Uber to improve and train their AI systems, subject to your settings and applicable law.
* Your personal data is subject to Uber's Privacy Policy, which can be found in the terms.
* In case of disputes, arbitration is required with class-action waivers. You have a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.

**Harmful Clauses:**

* **Arbitration:** As mentioned, you're required to use binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with class-action waivers. This means you'll have to negotiate with Uber directly, rather than going to court. Additionally, you won't be able to join a class-action lawsuit with others who have similar disputes.

Some good points to note about these terms include:

* Both Uber and you can terminate the agreement under certain conditions.
* You can find contact information for Uber's legal team in the terms, in case you have questions.

Overall, these terms seem to focus on Uber's use of user-submitted content and their privacy and arbitration policies.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — UBER US TERMS OF USE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Uber and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update revised arbitration after the New Jersey Uber Eats arbitration decision, added language on AI-generated trip summaries and driver/rider safety features, and expanded liability sections regarding third-party services.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Uber to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.uber.com/legal/en/document/?country=united-states&lang=en&name=general-terms-of-use . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.uber.com/legal/en/document/?country=united-states&lang=en&name=general-terms-of-use .

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** These Terms of Service apply to all products and services offered by Airbnb.

* **Termination:** The termination clause gives Airbnb the right to terminate your account at any time, with conditions described in the current Terms of Service document.

SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — AIRBNB TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Airbnb and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added new AnyWhere/Icons experience terms, revised cancellation and refund policies (including AirCover updates), added language on automated/AI-driven listing detection (e.g. anti-party tools), and updated arbitration provisions.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Airbnb to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/2908 . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/2908 .
